title: quercus novomexicana var. typica
intro: Quercus novomexicana var. typica, commonly known as New Mexico white oak, is a plant species that is native to the southwestern United States. This deciduous tree is valued for its timber and is also used in herbal medicine due to its potential health benefits. New Mexico white oak has been traditionally used to treat various ailments, including inflammation, fever, and digestive issues, thanks to its therapeutic actions as an anti-inflammatory, antipyretic, and laxative. The plant's bioactive constituents, which include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, contribute to its medicinal properties and have been studied for their antioxidant and antimicrobial effects.
